relay/upstream-drops-connection: 502 and x-sb-egress-error agree; only the free-text message of a transport failure differs (Bun's fetch wording vs the Rust client's)
tunnel/frame-too-large: frames pipelined with the open frame: Bun handles them before the connect finishes (error without a connected frame); Rust answers connected, then the same error
tunnel/starttls-on-plain-socket: same ordering difference (Bun also refuses startTls pipelined before connect even in starttls mode; Rust accepts it)
tunnel/head-not-json: Bun tcp.ts throws an uncaught SyntaxError and the egress process dies; Rust answers an 'expected tcp.open' error frame
ranges/table-pinned: INTENTIONAL: the Rust table has the 8 ranges added in sproutboat-packages#240; the Bun runtime in use predates it
intent/default-user-agent: INTENTIONAL: Bun sends 'User-Agent: Bun/<version>' when the app sent none; Rust sends none (as workerd)
intent/fetch-port-25: INTENTIONAL: Rust refuses fetch() to port 25 (as the tunnel does); the Bun service tries to connect
allow/*: INTENTIONAL: Rust parses SB_EGRESS_ALLOW (CIDR ranges, any spelling of an address); Bun compares answer text exactly
refuse-added/*: INTENTIONAL when the Bun runtime table predates sproutboat-packages#240 (these only run once it has them, and are then identical)
rebind/refused/mapped*: INTENTIONAL (D4): allowing 127.0.0.1 also allows its IPv4-mapped spelling (::ffff:7f00:1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1), the same destination; Bun compared text, so refused it
tls/https-to-plain-port: INTENTIONAL (D5): an https request to a server that never answers the handshake hangs in Bun (no timeout); Rust fails after the 10 s connect timeout
